findings.reason: the destructive pass would reach peer projects' run directories under a plan that scopes itself to reckon, so the node must be given the explicit `--project reckon --repo <reckon checkout>` form, or the section must say plainly that the pass is fleet-wide and the lead's authorisation covers it.
findings.text: the section says "for the reckon repository" but names the bare commands `reckon crew gc` and `reckon crew gc --apply`, and `--project` defaults to None meaning "all local ledgers by default" (`reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2030-2034`, and the module usage at `reckon/crew/gc.py:1783` reads "Retire finished crew run directories across every mounted project"), so the apply pass the node will run reclaims run directories belonging to every locally registered project — imas-efit and nova among them — which this plan's own record says its author has no authority over (f-tchhab-004: `crew/reports` for those projects is theirs to bound)

findings.reason: the sentence is the section's statement of what the apply pass can reach, and a node relying on it will neither anticipate the unledgered cohort nor be able to reconcile the observed drop with the count it expected, so the bound and the drop arithmetic must name both sweeps.
findings.text: "`garbage_collect` reclaims only directories the project's ledger knows (`gc.py` near line 767)" is false: the same `garbage_collect` call runs `_unledgered_run_directories` (`reckon/crew/gc.py:835` → `reckon/crew/routing.py:1949`), which removes run directories that no ledger knows, across the union of every registered mount's ledger, once they are past retention and hold no live pointer

findings.reason: the negative control as written does not cover the removals it is meant to bound, so it can report "no overlap" over a subset while a live-claimed or dirty tree was removed unobserved.
findings.text: the declared keep-guard check reads "the removal lines are checked against that list, with the check's output (no overlap) in the log", but only two removal prints exist (`removing run directory …`, `reckon/crew/gc.py:790-794`, and `removed worktree trash …`, `gc.py:139`); worktree releases record into `removed_worktrees` in the JSON report with no printed line (`reckon/crew/routing.py` has no `print` at all), and `_unledgered_run_directories` calls `shutil.rmtree` with no line either, so the check passes while the removal category the section exists to reclaim (106 worktrees) and the unledgered directory removals are never compared to the kept list

findings.reason: the node is told to compare a run-directory drop to a count the report does not emit, so it will either compare against the worktree figure or invent the count; the measure must name the row sets and keys it sums.
findings.text: "with the count it names as reclaimable beside the total" names no count the report actually has: `counts.reclaimable` is computed over worktrees only (`reckon/crew/gc.py:902`), while run directories are reported per row by `action` (`run_directories`, `unledgered_run_directories`) with a `run_directories_withheld` total and no reclaimable total

findings.reason: the population is independently justified by real walkers (the gc sweeps themselves iterate `runs_root`) and by the 22,377 measured directories, so correcting the citation changes the rationale's accuracy but no step, measure or write path in the section.
findings.text: "Readers that walk that population, such as the runs-root stamp in `recovery_watch.py` (near line 3027) … pay for every directory in it" mis-cites its first example: line 3027 is `file_stamp(runs.runs_dir())` and `file_stamp` is a single `Path.stat()` of the root (`reckon/capabilities.py:1292-1299`), so that reader pays one stat whatever the population holds and does not walk it
